content: {"rules": ["Model forecasts tend to overshoot true prices, especially in early periods of the 30-day horizon.", "Sentiment signals with positive values correlate with higher forecasted prices but do not reliably prevent subsequent price corrections.", "Forecasts show diminishing accuracy as the 30-day horizon extends, indicating potential lag or model drift.", "True prices often exhibit mean-reversion after initial spikes, contradicting the model’s upward trend assumptions.", "Model bias is more pronounced when sentiment is neutral or negative, leading to overconfidence in price continuation.", "Forecast accuracy improves when recent sentiment is consistently positive and prices are trending upward.", "Model forecasts should be adjusted downward if true prices show sharp divergence from forecasted values within the first 10 days.", "Sentiment and price behavior are not perfectly aligned; forecasts may ignore sentiment-driven volatility or reversal signals."]}
